verdicts.reason: Both share the same broken skeleton. The CTA pill sits flush against the headline's left edge and comes first in reading order, the three steps are microscopic fragments scattered out of sequence (one at the top, two stacked on the left) and the footer legal line is illegible. A is slightly worse because its headline wraps with an orphaned 'cup' on line two, while B's 'Three steps to a / better cup' break is balanced.

A has a sensible banner flow (bag on the left, headline in the centre with a balanced wrap, CTA on the right with clear space). However, the three steps are unreadable micro-text across the top in reversed order (03, 02, 01), and the bag is cropped at the left edge. B jams the CTA against the headline, leaves an orphaned 'cup' and scatters illegible steps out of order, so it is a jumbled copy.

A keeps a left-to-right order (bag, headline, CTA), but the bag touches the left canvas edge, 'cup' is orphaned and the headline nearly touches the CTA. Its steps are also unreadable fragments scattered around the CTA (01 above, 02 below, 03 bottom centre). B wraps the headline well, but it puts the CTA first, butting directly into the headline, and its steps run as tiny unreadable text across the top in reversed order.

B has a balanced headline wrap, the bag inset from the edge, the eyebrow above the headline and a clear gap before the CTA, though its steps are illegible micro-text scattered around the CTA and out of sequence. A crops the bag against the left edge, orphans 'cup', runs the headline almost into the CTA and strings tiny unreadable steps along the top.
